title: Autonomy-First 90-Day Activation Toolkit: Manager Checklist and Impact Contract
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview:
This playbook provides a repeatable manager-led process for activating new individual contributors (ICs) and managers for immediate, measurable contribution within their first 90 days. The approach centers on "autonomy-first" enablement: clear success contracts, progressive handoffs of responsibility, and a calibrated feedback rhythm.

Purpose and audience:
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-impact while preserving onboarding quality and psychological safety.
- Audience: Hiring managers, onboarding buddies, people-ops partners, and hiring committees.

Principles (why this is different):
1) Autonomy with guardrails — new hires get early ownership with explicit success criteria and rollback gates.
2) Evidence-driven ramp — measure impact with observable outputs (code reviews, shipped experiments, customer tickets resolved).
3) Manager-as-enabler — managers set context, remove blockers, and check in on autonomy rather than micromanage.
4) Lightweight documentation — use short living "Impact Contracts" rather than long orientation decks.

Quick start (one-page):
1. Before day 1: hire packet sent, 90-day Impact Contract drafted by manager + people-ops template.
2. Day 0–7: orientation + role-specific kickoff; buddy assigned; initial micro-project defined.
3. Week 2–4: first delivery checkpoint (MVP or experiment).
4. Week 6: mid-point calibration with manager & people-ops; adjust contract.
5. Week 10–12: impact review and transition to steady-state responsibilities.

90-Day Impact Contract (template):
- Role: [short role summary]
- Context: [team mission and key dependencies]
- Three initial objectives (SMART):
  1) Objective A — success metric, deadline, owner (IC / manager split)
  2) Objective B — success metric, deadline
  3) Objective C — success metric, deadline
- Early ownership scope: [features/areas the hire will own within 30–60 days]
- Rollback gate: [conditions where ownership reverts to manager/support]
- Key stakeholders and communication channels: [names, Slack channels, weekly sync cadence]
- Review cadence: Week 2, Week 4, Week 6, Week 12

Manager checklist (pre-hire -> day 90):
- Pre-hire (48–72h before start):
  1) Draft Impact Contract and share with people-ops (owner: manager).
  2) Reserve first-week calendar blocks for 1:1s, team kickoff, and working session.
  3) Provision access to repos, infra, docs; create an initial starter issue in the tracker with context.
  4) Identify and brief buddy and key reviewers.
- Day 0–7:
  1) Kickoff meeting: review Impact Contract, team mission, and expected first deliverable.
  2) Provide a single micro-project with clear acceptance criteria (<=5 days of focused work).
  3) Ensure buddy shadowing on day-to-day tasks and codebase walkthrough.
- Week 2–4:
  1) Checkpoint 1: review micro-project output, provide concrete feedback using the rubric below.
  2) If on track, extend ownership to a small component; update contract.
  3) If off track, define a learning sprint with explicit success markers and resources.
- Week 6 (midpoint):
  1) Formal midpoint calibration: manager + IC + people-ops (15–30m).
  2) Validate 2 of 3 objectives have measurable progress or re-scope.
  3) Confirm psychological safety: ask about blockers, clarity, workload, and team dynamics.
- Week 10–12:
  1) Impact Review: summarize outputs vs. contract, recommended steady-state role, and competency gaps.
  2) Confirm promotion into autonomy (owner list, handoff notes, and access).
  3) Archive contract and capture lessons learned in team wiki.

Feedback and evaluation rubric (used at checkpoints):
- Categories (score 1–5):
  - Problem understanding (clarity on what problem is being solved)
  - Delivery quality (completeness, tests, docs)
  - Collaboration (proactiveness, responsiveness, cross-team communication)
  - Learning velocity (how quickly gaps are closed)
  - Impact (measurable outcome tied to objective)
- Guideline: 4+ indicates ready for independent ownership in that dimension; 3 means needs coaching; <=2 requires a remediation plan.

Sample remediation plan (if <=2 in any category at Week 4):
1) Define a focused learning sprint (2 weeks) with 3 concrete deliverables.
2) Assign a mentor and 2 pairing sessions per week.
3) Manager to provide weekly written feedback with examples.
4) Re-evaluate at end of sprint; escalate to people-ops if progress < 50% of target.

Communication templates (short examples):
- Day 0 kickoff email to team:
  Subject: Welcome [Name] — Role + First Week Plan
  Body: Hi all — please welcome [Name]. This week they will be focused on [micro-project]. Buddy: [Name]. 1:1s will be on [days]. Please add context to the starter issue: [link].
- Midpoint calibration invite:
  Subject: [Name] 6-week calibration: impact & blockers
  Body: Please join a 20m check-in to validate progress against the Impact Contract. Agenda: 1) progress 2) blockers 3) next 3 weeks.

Operational integrations and measurements:
- Track progress in a shared tracker (team project board) with an "Onboarding" swimlane.
- Metrics to monitor (people-ops dashboard):
  - Median time-to-first-merged-PR (goal: <= 21 days)
  - Fraction of hires meeting 2/3 objectives at Week 6 (target: >= 70%)
  - Manager satisfaction with onboarding (pulse survey at Week 4; target >= 85% positive)
  - New hire self-reported clarity score (Week 2 & Week 6; scale 1–5; target >= 4)

Roles and responsibilities:
- Manager: owns Impact Contract, blockers removal, weekly 1:1s, calibration.
- Buddy: domain orientation, code walkthroughs, quick questions.
- People-ops: template, escalation, pulse surveys, remediation support.
- Hiring committee: confirms scope and success markers for role prior to offer acceptance.

Escalation and exceptions:
- If a remediation sprint fails (progress < 50%), manager escalates to people-ops within 3 business days with written evidence and proposed next steps.
- For hires with visa/work-permit constraints or part-time schedules, adjust timelines proportionally and document exceptions in the Impact Contract.

Templates and artifacts (links to examples):
- Impact Contract template: /confluence/people-ops/templates/impact-contract
- Onboarding tracker board: /confluence/teams/<team>/boards/onboarding
- Week 4/6 feedback form (survey): /confluence/people-ops/forms/new-hire-pulse

Frequently asked questions (FAQ):
Q: What if the new hire doesn’t want early ownership?
A: Discuss preference in the initial 1:1; autonomy is a path, not a mandate — you can opt for a slower ramp while preserving the checkpoints. Update the contract accordingly.
Q: Do we use this for interns or contractors?
A: Yes. Adjust objectives to scope and duration; target a single deliverable within first 30 days for short-term engagements.

Appendix: Example Impact Contract (filled):
- Role: Backend Engineer — Realtime Inference Routing
- Context: Improve cold-start latency for streaming requests by optimizing request routing and caching.
- Objective 1: Implement and land a prefix-cache prototype (measure: 95th latency p95 <= 150ms for sample workload) — due Week 4 — owner: IC (with mentor pairing).
- Objective 2: Add automated e2e test and perf benchmark for routing layer (measure: test coverage and benchmark output) — due Week 6 — owner: IC.
- Objective 3: Document rollout procedure and rollback checklist — due Week 12 — owner: manager + IC.
- Early ownership scope: routing service namespace, two endpoints, and the routing test harness.
- Rollback gate: If perf regression >10% in staging benchmarks after prototype, revert to manager-led iteration.
